blocks.x: 1. Study this lesson by answering all questions.

When meeting people for the first time, we often learn their names and a brief introduction to their backgrounds. After more time is spent with these new people, a deeper relationship grows as we learn more about their thoughts and character. We are also able to learn about people through others who are close to them. Similarly we will learn about Jesus the more we seek to know him, spend time with him, and have fellowship with other believers.
Before studying this course, who did you say Jesus was?

It is possible to have different perceptions about Jesus. Therefore to know what kind of person he was, we need to know his stories and to hear the opinions of those who were close to him. No one in all of history has had such an impact on this world as Jesus

Christ did. No one in all of history lived a completely sinless life, died on a cross, rose from the grave, and conquered death. Jesus’ death is an astonishing expression of his love for us. However if the death of Jesus on the cross marked the end of his life, he would have eventually become a vague memory, no different than any other great historical figure.
Indeed the Bible clearly shows that Jesus not only died on the cross but that he also rose from the dead. Jesus was resurrected and is still alive and relevant to us today. Praise the Lord!

There are some people who acknowledge that Jesus existed, lived his life, and then died. These same people choose to reject the truth and power of the resurrection; hence they are unable to know Christ fully.

Christ prophesied of his resurrection while he was ministering among the people. Furthermore the resurrection was the crux or central point of the disciples’ testimony. A. Defining Quiet Time

When we receive Christ and become a Christian and also have an assurance of salvation, a personal relationship is formed with Christ. Just as we need to associate with people to deepen our relationships, a personal fellowship with Christ is necessary to deepen our relationship with him.
The time when such association is made on a personal basis is referred to as either Quiet Time (QT) or time of devotion.
Jesus close to you? Do you meet him regularly? Quiet Time provides a way to be with him. Let us look to Jesus and his example of Quiet Time.
How did Jesus spend his day? Matthew 4:23
How do you spend your day? Write down your responses, and write the things you do in the order of most time spent.
Even with his busy schedule, what did Jesus still make an
important priority to? Luke 5:15-16.
Before Jesus started his day what did he do early in the morning?
Mark 1:35
How do you spend your morning?
David was a man who sought to please God (Acts 13:22). David
was able to please God because he had a deep fellowship with
God. Read Psalms 5:3 and 143:8, and summarize how David spent his times with God.
Quiet Time ● 25
This is what is referred to as a time of devotion or what is commonly called a Quiet Time (QT).
B. Reasons for Quiet Time
to the Christian
Why do Christians have QT? Why is it important to be quiet before God?
See the following for possible reasons Christians may have for spending
QT with God:

To have a personal relationship with God. The relationship with God cannot be broken once it is established (Romans 8:39). But to deepen this relationship, continuous fellowship is necessary. There are several ways of having fellowship with God; we can have a personal and intimate fellowship with him through QT.

To receive the guidance and protection of God. We will gain more knowledge and understanding of him as he provides insight and answers to problems in our daily lives through his Holy Spirit and his word.
How do the following verses describe the guidance and
protection of God?
a) Psalm 119:105
b) Psalm 119:133
God provides concrete answers to the problems in our daily lives through
QT.
To learn how to be more like Christ in his character, personality, and life
(2 Corinthians 3:18). For Christians to be the ‘salt and light’ of the world and spread the gospel, we should be true examples of the Christian faith.
We need a personal relationship with God if we desire for our lives and personality to be transformed.

To carry out the Lord's work (Luke 5:15-16; Mark 1:35). To do the works assigned in the church and to carry out the duty of spreading the gospel in the world, it is imperative to receive power and direction through fellowship with God.
C. Preparation for Quiet Time
1. Your Mind
You are about to have fellowship with God, the Almighty Creator.
Prepare your mind with expectation and fear. In this case, the fear is related to reverence to God. It is a combination of love and respect for an awesome God.
2. The Bible and QT Notebook
Open your Bible to the passage on which you will meditate for the day's
QT. We recommend you to have QT systematically. Once you start a book in the Bible for your QT, continue the book until you finish it.

Normally one paragraph is appropriate for a day's QT. If it is too short, you can continue to the next paragraph. If it is too long, you can stop in the middle of the paragraph. Be flexible on the amount for a day's
QT. Sometimes the Holy Spirit teaches enough lessons from one verse. If that is the case, stop there and continue with the remaining verses on the next day.

Be ready to write down what the Holy Spirit impresses on you in your QT notebook. Use the format provided at the end of this lesson for recording your insights. Do not use any secondary material for your QT.
You need to have direct fellowship with the Holy Spirit through his word.
3. Place and Time

The place for your QT is very important. You want to have a personal fellowship with the Lord, and you do not want to be disturbed. Find a place where you can spend twenty to thirty minutes with God without any disturbance.

Time often plays a crucial role in having consistent QT. Usually early morning is the most appropriate time for QT because you can start a new day with his guidance. However the time for QT is flexible depending on one’s situation. The important thing is to make sure the time for QT is not sacrificed because of other urgent matters in your life and ministry.
Quiet Time ● 27
D. Suggested Method for Quiet Time
The purpose of QT is not to understand the Scriptures thoroughly but to have God speak to you through his word. You can start QT using the following steps:
1. Praise God
Start your QT with praise. To praise God means to commend him for all that he has done. Please read Psalm 59:17 for an example of praising God.
You can praise God in prayer, while singing songs at church, while listening to praise music, or while meditating on the Psalms, such as
Psalm 98. Praise prepares the heart to go before God.
2. Depend on the Holy Spirit
The Holy Spirit is the author of the Bible, which was written through his inspiration. Therefore he illumines us to understand the Scriptures.
3. Find Truths by Meditating on the Word

God wants to reveal himself to us through the Scriptures (giving comfort, hope, warning, direction, etc.). Therefore we need to meditate on the words he gives us each day. During your QT, read the given text several times. Read his words with humility before God and the respect for his authority. Also, the more we meditate upon God’s word, the more our minds become focused on his eternal truths.
Meditate on the Scripture and find his eternal truths like the following:
1) Sins to confess
2) Promises to keep
4) Actions to take
5) Knowledge on God, Jesus Christ, or the Holy Spirit

Remember an English word, SPEAK. Allow the Holy Spirit to SPEAK to you through his word. The Holy Spirit sometimes may illumine several truths from one verse, and sometimes none. Remember that you do not have to understand everything in the passage, but you need to listen to what the Holy Spirit is speaking to you through the passage at that moment. You may have to read the same verse several times over in order to find truths. This may seem repetitive at first, but as you become familiar with the method, you will be able to find truths more quickly. It takes time to make the method yours, do not give up!
4. Apply It Practically
In Psalm 119:15, 97, meditation on the word is emphasized. What
is the difference between meditating and just reading?

Meditating on the word without application is like a tree without fruit. For the word to be “a lamp to my feet and a light to my path,” you need to apply the word to your life. Applying is reflecting upon and incorporating into your life these new insights, as well as relating to people and events with the truths which you have found. The following three elements are necessary for an effective application.
1) It should be personal
2) It should be practical.
3) It should be possible.
5. Pray about the Results of the Word
Ask for God's help to submit to what the word has said to you.
6. Share the Experience

Tell others about the changes that have taken place in your life as a result of applying God’s word. While sharing with others the grace that God has given us, our relationship will become warmer and deeper.

The method introduced here is a small but very helpful way to grow in spiritual maturity. Over time you may develop your own methods that will be more useful for you. Slowly, but steadily, walk with the word.
You will enjoy an abundant life and live in a manner that pleases God.
Read Colossians 1:10-12.
E. Some Helps on Quiet Time
It is not easy to have a QT regularly even though we know its benefits.
Think through the following helps to encourage a faithful and regular QT:

Frequent church meetings and worship at home may also be a help in establishing a steadfast QT.
3. Continuity

Sometimes you may find yourself going without QT for several days or even months. It is time to restart. Think about the value and importance of the word of God in your life. Especially think of the personal fellowship with the Almighty God through his word and start again with prayer.

Your confident and positive answers indicate that you are sure of your salvation. Becoming a Christian involves receiving Jesus Christ by faith.
It is the gift of God's love and forgiveness. It results in a threefold commitment of a person to Christ of one’s intellect, emotions, and will.
In other words, it is a commitment of the whole being.

Our relationship with Christ can be analogous to the concept of marriage, which must also contain the same three ingredients. For example, a man may be convinced intellectually that the woman who is his intended bride is the “right” spouse for him. He may be involved emotionally and love her with all his heart, but marriage requires more than the intellect and the emotions. It also involves the will. Not until the man and the woman, as an act of the will, commit themselves to each other before a minister do they become husband and wife. The two words,
“I do,” make all the difference.

So it is with your relationship with Jesus Christ. It is neither enough to believe intellectually in Christ, nor is it enough to have an emotional experience. Though both are valid, you do not become a
Christian until, as an act of the will, you trust Jesus Christ as your Savior and Lord. Let us examine each of the three elements of Christian commitment.

A. Commitment of the Intellect

Christianity is not “a blind leap of faith.” It is built upon historical facts, documented by centuries of scholarship and research. Many leading scholars have dedicated their lives to investigating the life, teachings, death, resurrection, and influence of Jesus of Nazareth. As a result, we have more historical evidence proving his resurrection than we have proof that Napoleon was defeated at Waterloo.
This good news of Jesus Christ’s resurrection was the message of the revolutionary New Testament church. It is still a revolutionary message today. It is a fact of history.

In order to make an intellectual commitment, we need to have a clear understanding of the gospel recorded in the Bible. Now let us determine if we have understanding of both the gospel and its historical facts.

B. Commitment of the Emotion
An emotion is a feeling or reaction to a specific act, event or experience.

Having been created with emotions, we experience emotional reactions in the process of hearing the gospel of Jesus, coming to know him, and believing in him. However the failure to distinguish between different emotions has caused many people to be confused in their relationship with
God.
1. Emotion Varies

As human beings, emotions are a normal part of our lives. Different personalities obviously produce varying reactions. One person may have high emotional energy, while another may be calm and reserved. Because emotions vary greatly, they should not be depended upon. Even though we all need to experience God, seeking an emotional experience has caused many to lack the assurance of a vital relationship with God.
2. Emotion as a Result of Faith

Assurance is based on the authority of God's word. When you meet God's conditions, as revealed in his word, you can be assured that you are a child of God. The Christian lives by faith in the trustworthiness of God himself and his word.

The train diagram illustrates the relationship between fact (God and his word), faith (our trust in God and his word), and feeling (the results of our experience). Note the three components in the diagram. The engine is in the front to pull the train. The firebox that contains the heat source or fuel follows the engine. The last one is a caboose. The train will run with the power of steam produced in the engine using the heat source from the firebox. The engine cannot pull the train if the fuel is not provided. The train will run with or without the caboose, but it would be useless to attempt to pull the train by the caboose.

In the Christian life, fact is the engine, faith is the heat source, and feeling is the caboose. When we, as Christians, add our faith on the fact which is the word of God, our believing life can go forward. As the caboose cannot pull the train, we should not depend upon feelings or emotions. Instead, we must place our faith in the trustworthiness of God and the promises of his word.
C. Commitment of the Will

In addition to the intellect and emotions, becoming a Christian and being certain that you are a Christian involves the will. Christ emphasized the importance of one’s will in relation to the assurance of salvation. A
Christian must make a conscious commitment to believe in and to follow

D. Threefold Confirmation
God gives us a threefold confirmation that Christ is in our lives.

We have the external evidence of the word of God. Assurance is based on the authority of God's word.
2. The Holy Spirit

3. Changed Life
What is the final source of confirmation that Christ is in our lives?
The proof that we have experienced a new birth and have become children of God will be demonstrated by our changed lives.
E. Dealing with Doubts

The enemy (Satan) desires that we doubt our salvation so as to make us discouraged in our faith and walk with the Lord. Knowing how to deal with these doubts is very critical to our consistent growth in spiritual maturity. Reading, studying, memorizing, applying God’s word, being attentive to the Spirit’s work in our lives, and remembering the ways God is changing our lives are all important weapons against doubt. Another important weapon against doubt is to know how to deal with sin and guilt in our lives that is through confession of sin. Confession of our sin to God needs to be a regular part of our walk with him.

To make forgiveness a reality in your life each and every day, confess your sin to God by:

 Thanking him for his forgiveness…thanking him demonstrates your faith and that it is true for you.

Another important step! If you have sinned against someone, then go to this person and ask forgiveness for the wrong you have done. This will go a long way in helping to restore any broken relationship.

God? Take a few moments right now and confess it to God and remember to thank him for his forgiveness!

We have entered into a special relationship with God because we now believe in Jesus. We know with certainty that we are God's children and we believe that we will live with him forever. The Holy Spirit counsels us to have such faith (Romans 8:16), but as we begin our spiritual journey with this personal conviction, we need objective facts about the God in whom we have placed our faith. Abstract and philosophical conceptions of God will no longer suffice. We need to know our God more deeply.
Only with clearer knowledge will our faith become stronger.
As Christians, we already know God. However if God is to be the constant center of our lives, we need to know more about God's attributes.
Only then will we be able to live in a manner pleasing to God. The Bible teaches very specifically about God's attributes.

Many people live a life of doubt and unbelief because they do not know God's character. Knowing God is very important as we live our lives. If we do not know him, it is easy to commit wrong, since it is difficult to understand the circumstances and direction of our lives without the knowledge of God. The mightiest thoughts the mind can entertain are the thoughts of God. But our ideas concerning God should correspond to that which is true of God. Only then can we truly worship and lead a genuine Christian life.

A. The Attributes Unique to God
greatness
The following attributes are those that belong to God exclusively so that there is nothing resembling them in a created being or spirit.
1. God Is Sovereign
The word sovereign means “chief, highest or supreme.” When we say that

In Romans 11:36, how is God's sovereignty described?

The Bible is a compilation of books written by around forty authors in a period spanning 1,500 years. The Old Testament is the word that Moses and the prophets received from God. It has been handed down orally or in writing through history. The Pentateuch was established as the authorized version in the fifth century BC; the books of the prophets and the books of literature in the second century BC. The Old Testament is composed of thirty-nine books and is written mostly in Hebrew.
The New Testament is a compilation of books and letters written by the disciples who were inspired by God. Recognition of a formal canon of the

New Testament did not occur until long after the time of its writing. The collection and recognition of all the New Testament books was a gradual process. During the first century of the church (from Pentecost to about
AD 140), there was only a very slow distribution and recognition of the writings that later were brought together and recognized as inspired. After

AD 140 a more rapid recognition of the canonical books occurred. By the end of the second century almost all of the books were known and recognized as authoritative. Finally, by the end of the fourth century the official canon of the New Testament was recognized and fixed.

Why did it take so long for the authority of all the New Testament books to be acknowledged by the church? First, the New Testament church already had a canon of Scripture—the Old Testament—which was considered all that was needed in the church ―for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16).
Second, as long as the apostles were alive, there was little felt need for an authoritative body of writings. The early church already had the
Old Testament and the living apostles to teach them (Acts 2:42). There was no urgency to copy and distribute the New Testament books so that they could be widely known and acknowledged.

Third, the recipients of the New Testament books were spread all across the Mediterranean basin. It is likely that churches would share with other churches any authoritative books that they received from the apostles. But because of poor communication and the slow production of books, no single church would always know about all of the apostolic writings in existence. Churches would receive various portions of the
New Testament without knowing what portions other churches possessed.
The New Testament is composed of twenty-seven books and was, in the original manuscripts, written entirely in Greek.
The Bible’s purpose is not only to educate us or give us mere knowledge, but it is also to teach us knowledge about the saving grace of God and how to walk with God in our daily lives.

This is also true spiritually. If a person memorizes, studies, reads, hears the word, and then meditates on it, his or her grasp of the Bible becomes solid. Reading is faster than studying and provides the big picture, but careful and detailed study will help you to think, to remember, and to apply. Christians can use some Bible study aids such as study Bibles, Bible dictionaries, Bible handbooks, and maps. However use commentaries with discernment. Although they can be helpful, you can become overly dependent upon them.
D. Memorize the Word

By guarding it according to your word.
Your testimonies are my heritage forever, for they are the joy of my heart. (Psalm 119:9, 111)

Matthew 4:4, 7, 10

"Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly" means?
I know of no form of intake of the word which pays greater dividends for the time invested than Scripture memory. (Dawson
Trotman)

Scripture memorization is very important. God calls us to commit his truth to memory that we might have more understanding of himself. There are many different ways to go about memorizing Scripture: write out the verse several times, repeat the verse out loud, read it over and over, etc.
Not everyone memorizes in the same way or in the same amount of time, so it is not the method that matters, only that the verses are memorized.

E. Meditate on the Word

Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked, nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the seat of scoffers; but his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night. (Psalm 1:1-2)

Prayer is how the power of God is unleashed. Personal battles and battles for others are won in prayer, and the cause of Christ is thus furthered. God does not require us to have great faith; however we are to have faith in our great God. A life of faith is experienced only by those who walk in obedience to the Lord. When a person truly has faith in the only great
God, that person will delight in both trusting and obeying God..

By faith we receive the answer to our requests. If you know that you are abiding in Christ, that you are controlled by the Holy Spirit, and that you are praying according to the word and will of God, you can expect God to answer your prayers, so be prepared to receive answers.

is new. Also, note what applications you can make to your life.
Lesson
Fellowship
1. Take sermon notes during a worship service.
2. Read Philippians.
3. Study this lesson.
4. Memorize Romans 12:4-5 and John 13:34-35.
5. Have Quiet Time regularly.
6. Memorize the names of the books in the Old
Testament from Genesis to Proverbs.
Fellowship involves meeting people and developing relationships with them. Christians need such relationships. However the fellowship of

Christians has characteristics that are not found in the relationships of the world. The relationships in the world normally begin when individuals start associating with one another from a safe and appropriately maintained distance. The fellowship of Christians, on the other hand, began with the cross where Christ already accomplished the work of breaking down relational barriers (Ephesians 2:13-14). This fellowship of

Christians is not a building or organization but a community of believers called the body of Christ. True fellowship begins with and is brought to its fullness through Christians coming together in worship.
A. Fellowship Through Worship
worship elements included in a worship service

Many churchgoers believe that one goes to worship services mainly to listen to the sermons. Though it is an important part of worship, listening to the sermon is not the whole of worship. One does not worship for oneself but for God. It is through worship that one can have fellowship with God and other members of the body of Christ.
What does God desire or insist as we worship him?
Leviticus 10:3
God is pleased when a community of believers comes to him in worship, desiring to praise his name and his glory. Our attitude in worship is important if we are to worship God in truth.
John 4:24 commands us to worship God in “spirit and truth.” What

kind of attitude of worship should we have if we are to obey this command? Record your thoughts after considering what this means and how it can affect your life. Write down how you can apply this to your worship life.
Psalm 95:6 and Ecclesiastes 5:1-2 teach us about the outward
attitudes of a worshipper. List them.
Worship does not need to be complex. But during worship, we must give
God our hearts and our lives; we must desire to enter God's presence.
Acts 2:42 teaches about the four elements needed in worship.
What are they?
What are some other elements of true worship?
1 Chronicles 16:29; Colossians 3:16; Psalm 47:1-2, 5
Praise is one of the important components of the worship we lift up to
God.

1. By praising God, we proclaim the absolute trust we have placed in the God of our salvation. By praising God, we can also put on the shield of faith against the attacks of the devil, and allow God to display his power.
2. Praise frees up our lives for the work of the Holy Spirit.
Sometimes, praising precedes the renewing work of the Holy
Spirit.
3. Praise contributes to the unity of the saints.
4. Praise prepares us to fix our hearts on God and to turn an attentive ear to him. It also paves the way for God who desires to pour out his love on us.
5. We get a foretaste of heaven as we enter God's presence in praise.
B. The Fellowship of Christians
1. Be Members of One Another
So we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another. (Romans 12:5)

If it is true that everyone is equal under the cross, every Christian has the privilege of becoming an integral member of the family of God. In the family of God, we must be willing to learn from one another and to encourage one another. The fellowship of the saints can fully develop only when Christians are diligent in building one another up. We cannot participate in this fellowship while isolating ourselves from the community of saints. God desires that all Christians become active members of God's family by joining a local church. The New Testament states that Christians are “members one of another.” Paul used an illustration to get this point across—the human body.
Read 1 Corinthians 12:14-27. Summarize the conclusion Paul
comes to in these verses. 1 Corinthians 12:27
2. Be United in Christ
There is one body and one Spirit—just as you were called to the one hope that belongs to your call— (Ephesians 4:4)
The human body is not made up of separate and individual members.
Rather, the body exists as a unified whole of many parts that are members of one body. Similarly, the church is not an association of individual
Christians but is the body of Christ, consisting of people who are members of one another from the inception of their Christian lives.
In its broadest sense, the body of Christ is the historical and global community of the saints. The Bible frequently teaches about the body of
Christ in the context of a specific local church community. Hence
Christians must participate in the life of a local church and joyfully take on their respective roles as members of the body.

Satan’s strategy involves destroying unity among Christians. He is the author of confusion, insensitivity, and false doctrines. In the Bible, we discover the power whereby Satan's strategy can be defeated.
What did Jesus make a request to the Father in his prayer?
John 17:11

It is the power of “one-mindedness” in the body of Christ. This unity among Christians reveals the essence of the gospel; and that essence comprises the fact that “in Christ God was reconciling the world to himself.” (2 Corinthians 5:19) Christ was indeed God in the flesh. He was, and is, one with the Father. If unity is destroyed in Christ's body, then the most powerful means of communicating the gospel to lost souls that

Christ is God are destroyed. The ingredient in the church that convinces non-Christians that Jesus is God is unity—living in “such harmony with one another.” This, in a sense, represents a miracle because humans generally move toward disunity. When non-Christians see true unity and true oneness, their hearts cry out to partake of that kind of love (John
Read John 17. Which of the following is NOT something Jesus
prayed for in John 17:?
a) That the disciples may experience his joy
b) That the disciples may experience the same unity as the
Father and Son
c) That the disciples may have the glory the Father gave to the
Son
d) That the world may experience his joy, glory, and unity
3. Accept the Differences of One Another
But grace was given to each one of us according to the measure of
Christ's gift. (Ephesians 4:7)

All believers have been made one in the body of Christ, but there is still great diversity among Christians. We must understand and accept the many differences found among the members of the body if we are to be
Christ's unified body.
a. We Have Received Different Gifts
Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us…
(Romans 12:6a)

The gift of salvation is from the one Holy Spirit, but he also gives other gifts. According to Paul, some were given the gift of teaching, others the gift of service, and some the gift of exhortation. The Holy Spirit desires these different gifts to be used in unity, for the building and edifying of the body of Christ, and not for comparing and criticizing.
List the gifts from Romans 12:6-8.
b. We Have Been Given Different Levels of Faith
Let not the one who eats despise the one who abstains, and let not the one who abstains pass judgment on the one who eats, for God has welcomed him. (Romans 14:3).

If we are mature Christians, we will be sensitive toward our brothers and sisters in Christ who may not be as spiritually mature. We will be careful not to do anything that may cause them to stumble and fall into sin. If these two attitudes are working concurrently in a local body of believers, unity will emerge.
c. We Have Different Personal Backgrounds

After this I looked, and behold, a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands, and crying out with a loud voice, “Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!” (Revelation 7:9-10)

Prejudice, favoritism, and discrimination in the body of Christ violate the laws of God. Furthermore, they violate the nature of the functioning body of Christ. We are all one. Every member is important—rich or poor, young or old, black or white, weak or strong, Jew or Gentile. If we show favoritism or judge people by outward appearances, we also destroy the unity, harmony, and oneness in the body of Christ which Christ and Paul both prayed and commanded.
Ephesians 2:11-12. Cultural, racial, national, and religious barriers are broken down when people are brought near to God by the blood of Christ.

Enemies may experience peace and reconciliation when they come together as members of the body of Christ. All believers have the same access to God the Father because the same Spirit dwells in them. Together, we are being built into a dwelling place of God.
Consider and record your responses to the following: “Enemies

may experience peace and reconciliation when they come together as members of the body of Christ.” Think of an enemy you have (or had). How could being a member of the same body of Christ help you reconcile with that enemy and come back together in fellowship?
4. Love One Another
A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. (John

This exhortation introduces another model by which our understanding of the functioning church is enriched. The concept of the family adds a dimension of warmth, concern and loyalty. The term “brotherly love” refers to the love that should coexist within family units. Applied to the church, it refers to the love Christians should have for each other as brothers and sisters in Christ. We are the family of God. We have all been
“born again” into God's eternal family.
How should true love be expressed? 1 John 3:18
How did the first century church express its love? Acts 4:32
5. Edify the Church
Therefore encourage one another and build one another up.
(1 Thessalonians 5:11)

Paul commended the Thessalonian Christians for their concern and love for one another. They had learned the importance of mutual encouragement, exhortation, and comfort. He knew the primary means of encouragement—God's truth. “We also thank God constantly for this, that when you received the word of God, which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men but as what it really is, the word of
God, which is at work in you believers.” (1 Thessalonians 2:13)

Christians must be ready to share the word with others who are in special need of encouragement. But we cannot encourage one another with Scripture if we are not familiar with Scripture. Therefore every believer should study the word of God, not only for their personal growth but also for assisting others in their growth.
6. Conclusion

In the “body of Christ,” the church, every member must contribute to its continual growth. The church should be a group of people who believe in the word, who believe in the God of the Bible, who love and care for one another, and who want all people to be saved and experience fellowship with God and with other believers. This is what Jesus prayed during his ministry on earth.

I do not ask for these only, but also for those who will believe in me through their word, that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me. (John 17:20-21)

Lesson
Witnessing
1. Take sermon notes during a worship service.
2. Read 1, 2, and 3 John and Jude.
3. Study this lesson.
4. Memorize Romans 1:16 and 1 Peter 3:15.
5. Have Quiet Time regularly.
6. Memorize the names of the books in the
Old Testament from Ecclesiastes to Malachi.
7. Write your own salvation testimony.

After creating the universe, God gave an important commission to mankind: “And God blessed them. And God said to them, ‘Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that moves on the earth.’” (Genesis 1:28) This ultimate command was given to everyone—believer, unbeliever, man, woman, and child.
Christians who believe in God as the Creator should wholeheartedly obey this command.
After his work on the cross and then his resurrection, Jesus gave an important commission to his disciples.

Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age. (Matthew
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.
(Acts 1:8)
This commission has been given exclusively to those who believe in Jesus.
A. Attitude Toward the World
We first need to have a biblical attitude toward the world in order to be an effective witness. The following are the three views on the relationship between the church and the world:
1. Antagonistic view - one of confrontation
2. Mediating view - one of compromise
3. Changing view - one of conquering
Among the three views, the changing view is the sound one which Christians should adopt. Christians have been called from the world to the body of Christ.
Examine the three world views listed above
and record your responses to the following:

Of the three, the changing view is taught as the sound one Christians should adopt. What are the dangers of antagonistic and mediating views, and why are they less appropriate for Christians? To help with your answer read
Romans 12:1-2.
God dwells among the people who have been sent into the world and not in buildings which are separated from the world. (Thomas
Gillespie)
B. Attitude Toward Work

God does not limit his interest only to our “church” activities. He is equally interested in our painting and teaching as much as he is interested in how we pray, how we read the Bible, and how we praise him. God does not separate between the “secular” and “divine” because all things are under his authority. As God calls us into a relationship with him, we come to realize that we should use all our activities to praise God and to serve our neighbors. Instead of saying, “I am not a minister of God but a carpenter,” we should say, “I am doing the work of a disciple of Christ through carpentry.”
What was the consequence of Adam's disobedience?
Genesis 3:17-18
Work itself is not a result of sin. Work is a part of the principle of creation.
The result of Adam’s sin was that pain started to accompany the work which God had given.
How should we, as saved Christians, view work?
Colossians 3:22-23

As they become a new creation in Christ, Christians should change their views of their work in the world. Christians who witness need to understand the society in which they live and should actively participate in their work. These people can witness effectively as they bear witness to their societies as salt and light.
C. Witnessing the Gospel
words

Christians should share their faith in Jesus to nonbelievers so that they can also live a spiritually abundant life in Christ. To add validity to our witness, we should show them our devotion to Christ. It is necessary to learn the basic methods of witnessing. All of us can become an effective tool in God's hands as we train and gain experience.
1. The Challenge

Witnesses in a courtroom are expected to tell what they know about a given situation. The Christian witnesses are to tell others what they know about Jesus Christ and what it means to personally trust him.
What was the first thing Andrew did after he met Jesus?
What was Paul's message to the people? Acts 22:15
Of what was Paul not ashamed? Romans 1:16
And why?
2. Witnessing by Life
Since we are God’s children living in a warped and wicked age,
what kind of lives should we live? Philippians 2:15
How should we appear to the world?
In Matthew 5:16, what do people notice when a Christian's life
shines?
What can be the result?
You are writing a gospel,
A chapter each day,
By the things that you do,
And the words that you say.
People read what you write
Distorted or True.
What kind of gospel
Are you writing?
3. Witnessing by Word
The blind man whom Jesus healed had little or no theological
training, but he could give a simple and effective testimony. What facts did he relate? John 9:25
Read 1 Peter 3:15-16 and answer the following questions:
What precedes telling others about Christ?
What is “the hope that is in you”?
What would cause someone to ask you about the hope that is in
you?
What attitude should you have while witnessing?
4. Strategy for Witnessing situations

Jesus came to seek and to save the lost. Since he lives within us, we can simply ask him to give us the courage to speak for him. Whenever you are alone with a person for a few minutes, you can assume that you are there by divine appointment to share the good news of God's love and forgiveness. Though you should always seek to bring those who are interested to a definite commitment to Christ, you should not feel discouraged when some refuse to receive him as their Savior. That is
God's responsibility. It is your responsibility to tell them the good news with love and genuine concern.
We can set the following strategies according to the situation.
1. If it is difficult to have personal time, you can distribute tracks.
2. If you have 20-30 minutes of personal time, you can use Four
Spiritual Laws, Bridge Analogy, Evangelization Explosion, and other tools for witnessing.
3. If you can meet on a regular basis (workplace, church, etc.), you can have a personal Bible study with Unit I of this workbook.
Even though we use different strategies to reach others with the
gospel, the central message of the gospel should be same. What was the central message of Paul's witness?
1 Corinthians 1:23-24
Why is it important that we present Jesus Christ to people that
are lost? John 14:6; Acts 4:12
Although it is effective under the right circumstances, to share our experience, witnessing is about presenting a person—Jesus Christ—not a plan or a theory.
Read Acts 26:1-29 and summarize Paul’s testimony using the
three questions below. Then write your own testimony using the same questions as a guide.
a) What was your life like before you met Christ?
b) How did you meet him?
c) How has Christ transformed your life?
5. Witnessing as a Way of Life
Successful witnessing may be defined as simply taking the initiative to share Christ in the power of the Holy Spirit and leaving the results to
God (2 Timothy 4:2; Colossians 1:28-29). Here are some important reminders as you step out in faith to communicate Jesus Christ to others in your ordinary life.
1. Be prepared. You have to be prepared for God to use you as he wants.
2. Pray in the Spirit. It is our responsibility to share Christ with others and to pray for people to come to Christ. God is the

One who by his Spirit can produce faith in the hearts of men and women and change their lives. But we should not expect vague and superficial prayers to be answered. We should pray with an earnest love and desire for their salvation. Pray by mentioning their names individually and record when and how God answered your prayer.
3. Take the initiative. Regard the opportunities you have of meeting people as divine appointments. Consider the following:
a) Do not wait for people to come to you. Go to them with
the good news of Christ. God has already commanded us to go and tell the good news to all.
b) We witness because it is the command of Christ but we

should go further and make witnessing a regular part of our lives. As you come into contact with and meet people, witness to them. Show them your concern for them and naturally lead the conversation. The words Jesus said to the woman at the well (John 4:7) and what Philip said to the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8:30) are good examples.

4. Turn the conversation to Christ. Do not be too hasty! We need to show genuine interest in the person by listening to what he or she thinks or believes about the meaning and purpose of life. As we do this it opens the door to share about how Jesus gives meaning and purpose to our lives.
5. Expect results. When you witness, expect people to respond.
We should not base our expectation on our technique or beliefs but place our confidence in his love, his power, and his promise.

is new. Also, note what applications you can make to your life.

blocks.x: 1. Take sermon notes during a worship service.
2. Read Ephesians.
3. Study this lesson.
4. Memorize Ephesians 5:18 and Galatians
5. Have Quiet Time regularly.
6. Review the names of the books in the Old Testament from
Genesis to Proverbs.
A. Defining Being Filled with the Spirit
The Holy Spirit dwells in every believer. The Holy Spirit causes us to be

“born again” and empowers us to live a Christ-centered life. We cannot, through our own efforts, lead a Christ-centered life. We must ask, trust, and depend on the Holy Spirit to lead and guide us through our journey as Christians. This is called the Spirit-filled life.
Read John 14:16-17. Before Jesus left this earth what did he
promise to the disciples?
In John 14:18, Jesus says that he would not leave them as
orphans but would come to them. What do you think this means in relation to the promise he made?
In John 15:26, what does Jesus say about the ministry of the Holy
Spirit?
What explanation does Jesus give in John 16:14 regarding the
Spirit’s work?
Having answered the preceding questions, how would you
summarize the primary ministry of the Holy Spirit?
The word “filled” actually means to be directed and empowered by the
Spirit. Since the Holy Spirit came to glorify Christ (John 16:14) and is the

Spirit of Christ (Romans 8:9), to be filled with the Spirit is to be filled with or abiding in Christ. To abide in Christ is to live in dependence upon him, recognizing that it is his life, his wisdom, his resources, his strength, and his ability operating through you, which enables you to live according to his will. Christ lives in us and expresses his life through us by the power of his Spirit.
Ephesians 5:18 contrasts being filled with the Spirit to getting
drunk with wine. What kind of state is to be filled with the Holy
Spirit?

To be filled with the Spirit does not mean to be in a mystical state. Nor does it mean to be in an emotionally dry or highly intellectual state. The concept of the filling of the Holy Spirit from this verse stresses the abiding influence and power that the presence of the Spirit of Christ has in our lives and on our character.
B. Reasons to Be Filled with the Spirit
Spirit

As long as we are in this world and in our flesh, we cannot keep from sinning. Even if we believe in Jesus Christ and have begun a new life, we are still able to fall into sinful behavior (1 John 1:8). That is why the apostle Paul cried out, “Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body of death?” (Romans 7:24)
How does Galatians 5:17 describe this conflict?

A natural person can sometimes overcome this conflict with conscientious thoughts or ethical actions. However in our own power alone, we will fail spiritually. Our old selves cannot win this conflict because of our fleshly desires.
Read Romans 8:9-10, 13-14. What do Christians have to do to
win this conflict between the flesh and the Spirit?
Each person who claims to walk with Christ must be filled with the Holy
Spirit continuously—this leads to a victorious life.
C. Results of Being Filled with the Spirit
Spirit
In order to live a victorious life, we must be filled with the Holy Spirit.
We cannot overcome the power of Satan by ourselves. However through the power of the Holy Spirit we are able to overcome the power of Satan.
We have already learned that the primary ministry of the Holy Spirit is to reveal Jesus to us. The Holy Spirit impacts our lives by showing us who
Jesus is. As we focus on Jesus, we are able to become more like him.
Find the image of Jesus from Galatians 5:22-23 by listing the fruit
of the Spirit.

Through Jesus Christ, we can have victory over sin. Jesus himself lived a sinless life giving us the perfect example of how to live. It is important to build his character into our lives through the ministry of the Spirit so that we might live in a way that reflects Jesus.
We are meant to feel the impossibility of living the victorious life
in the strength of our flesh. When we try, we fail over and over.
Recall a time when you failed to live up to God’s standards; then record why you think you failed. What can you do next time to live victoriously?
D. Way of Being Filled with the Spirit

We have already learned that the filling of the Spirit emphasizes the abiding influence and power that his presence has in our lives and on our character. Nobody is able to change his or her character immediately. It takes time. As time goes by, our character should be transformed to that of Jesus. There is no single formula that can fill us with the Holy Spirit instantaneously. By having fellowship with the Holy Spirit, however, we can be gradually transformed into Jesus’ image.
Read 1 Corinthians 2:11-14. Write a brief summary of the
relationship of the Spirit and a person’s understanding of spiritual truth.
Now turn to 2 Timothy 3:16-17. After asserting that the word is
breathed out by God, Paul then says that the word has a specific purpose. What is it?

The Bible teaches us both about who God is and how we are to live a life that is pleasing to him. The word interacts with us, opening our eyes to see the wonder of the Savior, prompting us to obey him, convicting us when we do not, and guiding us to live a life that is pleasing to God. The word of God and the work of the Spirit are inseparable. The Spirit works in us and speaks to us through the word. Therefore we must have fellowship with the Holy Spirit through the word. The Holy Spirit illuminates Jesus and his character through the word. We are able to understand the way we should be through this fellowship. However simply understanding the way is not enough to change us.
What are our two responsibilities that Jesus mentioned in John
What is James’ encouragement in James 1:22?
a) Live out the message
b) Be courageous
c) Do not be timid
d) Love one another

After understanding his word, we need to apply it to our lives. In other words, we should obey through the guidance of the Holy Spirit. When we do this process (understand his way and apply it to our lives) continuously, we will be transformed into Jesus’ image and be filled with the Holy Spirit continuously. As a result, we will live in a manner that is pleasing to God.

There are many ways which help us to be filled with the Spirit and our personal Quiet Time is one of them. During QT, we find biblical truths and try to apply them to our lives. We try to obey the Holy Spirit through QT. Hence QT can be a good way to be filled with the Holy Spirit and maintain it for a victorious life. Start QT and continue it!

is new. Also, note what applications you can make to your life.

Even though Christians may live a Spirit-filled life, they cannot do away with sin while living in this world in their flesh (1 Corinthians 10:12).

Because the devil prowls around like a roaring lion seeking someone to devour, we must be on our guard at all times. However we cannot live a victorious life by our own power. God can shield and protect us from temptations and sin. We need to accept that it is God who gives us victory, and to depend upon him, his truth, and his strength to overcome all things.
A. Understanding Temptation
Corinthians 10:13 overcome you
In the Bible there are three similar concepts. Summarize them.
a) Trials (***James 1:2***-4)
b) Temptations (***James 1:13***-14)
c) Tests (Genesis 22:1)

Let us take some time now to study the subject of temptation. Christians can find a key solution to temptation in 1 Corinthians 10:13. Meditate on this verse for a few minutes and then answer the next several questions.
According to 1 Corinthians 10:13, what kind of temptations
overtake you?
Who enables you to endure it when you are being tempted?

b) Psalm 119:9, 11
Let us continue to apply these verses to our life.

B. Satan's Use of Temptation
strategies against the attacks, and use this information to live a victorious life

The ultimate source of all evil is Satan. But that does not mean that the devil always attacks us personally. Satan attacks us using every possible means including his direct involvement. We are attacked through three basic channels which Scripture calls the devil, the world, and the flesh. It is crucial, when you are being tempted, to determine what kind of temptation it is because each should be handled differently.
1. Attacks Us Directly

Scripture teaches that there is one personal supernatural spirit known as the devil or Satan, and there are many fallen angels known as the devil’s angels, or demons. This devil attacks directly to shake our relationship with God. When you are tempted to deny God's goodness, God's word, and/or God’s faithfulness, these are attacks directed at your God- awareness.
How did Satan attack Judas Iscariot? Luke 22:3; John 13:2

How does one handle a direct demonic attack upon God-awareness? First of all, one needs to acknowledge that the devil exists, and then one has to resist the devil (James 4:7). Let us study the best ways to resist the devil.
Christ gave us the perfect example of how to resist the devil.
In Matthew 4:4, 7, 10, what did Jesus use to resist the devil?

Jesus responded with the sword of the Spirit—the word of God. This is the best way to resist the devil. If the devil tempts you to doubt your salvation, you may rebuke his lies with the truth that leads to eternal life

(John 5:24; 1 John 5:13). Knowing and studying the Bible are so important, especially in dealing with temptations. That is why memorizing Scripture is also important. David said, “I have stored up your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.” (Psalm 119:11)
The more you study and master the word, the more you will be prepared to effectively deal with this type of temptation.
2. Through the World
Satan not only attacks us directly, but also indirectly through the world.
The kind of world we are talking about is “the world” God mentioned in

1 John 2:15-16 and “this world” mentioned in Romans 12:2. This kind of world refers to the world of unsaved people and the society, culture, and value systems they have established. The subtlest kinds of temptations are from this channel.
The world tempts us in what three areas? What are specific
examples of these? 1 John 2:16

An example: A young couple is very zealous for the Lord and then suddenly stops attending church. They purchased a new home and are now so busy decorating it that they have no time for God. They actually love the house more than they love God. That is sin and idolatry! The most difficult type of temptation comes from the world.
How does one handle this type of temptation? Read Matthew 6:19-

34. Probably this type of temptation—the world attacking the soul—will be the most prominent over the period of your life span. This is particularly true in our materialistic society. The tragedy of the modern church is that there are many who are called to faith, but few who are called to obedience. Faith that perseveres against the temptations of Satan through a Spirit-filled life is very precious. A willingness to follow and obey Jesus is needed for Christians to keep their faith actively working for God. To do his work, it is important first to follow him.
Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. (Matthew 4:19)
Following Jesus means that I accept his plans and perfect will. It also means I need to give my life unconditionally to him and obey him.

This teaching includes God’s gracious salvation from the penalty of sin plus provision for victory over sin after salvation—even the fullness of salvation that will still come to Israel when God fulfills his promises! Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. (Matthew 4:19)

To do the works of Jesus Christ, we must have a deeper fellowship with him and follow him. The training we have received so far shows its fruit in characteristic development and in the Lord's ministry. In this lesson we will study about the ministry.

There are still many people in churches who think they are living a Christian life by just listening to sermons from worship services. They have this passive attitude toward their life of faith because they have not been trained properly as Jesus’ disciples. When believers are trained, their attitude becomes more active. Therefore the fruit of training will result in the ministry for the Lord.

If the Reformation of the sixteenth century gave the Bible back to the church members, the spiritual reformation that is to come will return ministry to the church members. Francis Aeris said the following:
If we have been baptized, we are ministers whether we have been ordained as priests or not.

In this lesson we will look at five important elements to help the believers better understand their role in ministry. We will examine a biblical view of (1) the church, (2) the believers, (3) the gifts of God, (4) training, and
(5) the world. An understanding of these five elements will greatly assist believers to be spiritually effective in ministry.
A. Biblical View of the Church

The most challenging fact to Christians is not that I am to do something for the church but that I constitute the church. (F. C.
Mather)

In describing the relationship between the believers and the church, it is incorrect to say that the believers are “in” the church. It is equally wrong to say that the believers work “for” the church. Also, it is not biblical to say that believers work “in” the church.

between the believers and the church? Ephesians 2:20-22

Believers themselves “are” the church. So in order to know the believers’ ministry, it is necessary to know the ministry of the church. The two elements that make the church are service and fellowship. The church needs to carry out the ministries that Jesus did while he was on the earth in order to function as the body of Christ.

related to the commission given to the church?

b) _______________ (Spreading the gospel, foreign mission)

All ministries should begin at the church which represents the body of

Christ. Ministry should be conducted by individual members for individuals and to individuals, and should be transmitted to those outside the church as well. Therefore the church must carry out these three ministries—teaching, preaching, and healing—when members gather together. Individuals must carry out these duties in the world as they are dispersed in the world.
B. Biblical View of the Believers
commission of Jesus Christ
We often hear people saying, “But I am only a member of this church.”
This might sound very humble, but they have not properly understood the commission of Jesus. The Bible tells us that every Christian is a minister.
Church members are not the objects of ministry, as is often understood, but are the subjects of church ministry.

C. Biblical View of the Gifts of God
you have

God commands us to do his ministry, but he also gives us the gifts that we need in order to carry out his ministry. We should neither be proud of them as if they were ours, nor should we fail to use them. Gifts are freely given by God for his ministry. Gifts are to be used for the glory of God.
There are passages about gifts in Romans 12:6-8, 1 Corinthians
12:8-11, and Ephesians 4:11. Among these, the seven gifts mentioned in Romans are those that are easily seen in our everyday life. Explain each gift briefly.

gift(s) to use and that we are to be using that gift(s) accordingly.
Record your thoughts on what gift(s) you may have. How can you find a way to practice your gift to edify others?
D. Biblical View of Training
for the Lord

Gifts are essential to do the ministry of God. But for that gift to bear fruit, training is needed. It is wrong for a church to give someone an important role without training that person first. Those who desire to serve God should make necessary preparations. Training that is in line with the gift becomes an appropriate preparation for the church ministry.

Two inherent problems that our churches have are (1) there are not many pastors who want to train the believers and (2) there are few believers who desire to receive training. Some people think training is difficult and still others think that it is unnecessary. However the training for believers is imperative for a church to become a fully functioning, spiritually effective church.
How did Jesus train his disciples (Mark 3:13-15)? How can this
be applied to the church today?

There are several fields in which believers should be trained.
1. Devotional: Spending time with God, memorizing verses, etc.
2. Evangelism: Personal evangelism, evangelical Bible study, etc.
3. Encouragement: Building up and edification
4. Counseling: Family, marriage, adolescent, etc.
Consider the following suggestions for an effective training.
1. Never lose the commission as a worker
2. Look for people who are ministering with similar gifts
3. Read and study the Bible and other books which are necessary for ministry
4. Think of ways of using the gifts you have received
5. Start humbly even though you might have much experience in church life
6. Join a group that will challenge you in your dedication

to fulfill his commission
For trained believers to minister, they need to understand their field of ministry. Many Christians limit the scope of ministry to inside the church.

But the field of our ministry is this world. The world in which we live and work is where we should minister. Many believers limit their field to the region or country they belong to. But our scope of ministry is to the end of the earth (Acts 1:8). By broadening our vision of the world, it helps us to have a greater sense of God’s heart for the whole world.
